title: Epic says its new vibe-coded Epic Games Launcher is faster than Steam
gist: Epic released a public Preview of a ground-up, AI-assisted ('vibe coded') Epic Games Launcher marketed as faster than Valve's Steam, with Ars confirming a few seconds faster cold start. The release coincides with Tim Sweeney's pivot of Epic toward AI acceleration, aimed at building more rather than doing the same with fewer people.

insights.claim: Epic rewrote its Epic Games Launcher from scratch in a different tech stack, using AI to write and review features, so that a small team could ship across Windows, Mac and eventually Linux faster.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: AI coding is being used for a full rewrite of a production consumer product, a signal of enterprise adoption and shrinking engineering team size needs.
insights.quote: made us more efficient and allowed a small team to rewrite the code base

insights.claim: Epic is positioning the vibe-coded launcher as faster than Steam, and Ars testing found cold start to the store page a few seconds faster than Steam, while the claimed 0.06-second tray restore advantage is unnoticeable.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Speed is Epic's differentiator vs Steam; marginal gains in some metrics, so real competition is on features and catalog.

insights.claim: Epic said in June that the new Launcher V2 would have 5x faster cold start, and the Preview has bugs and is light on features, lacking certain social features and account management options.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Feature parity is incomplete, so adoption depends on closing gaps with the legacy launcher.

insights.claim: The Preview adds long-requested features including a Recent Games list and a centralized downloads hub.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Feature additions could help it win users from Steam.
insights.locator: That said, the new Preview launcher adds

insights.claim: The term vibe coding still carries heavy connotations of thrown-together slop that could hide crucial errors, which Epic acknowledged by warning of bugs in the Preview.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Quality perception is a reputational risk to AI-assisted shipping; monitor bug reports during the Preview.

insights.claim: A Bloomberg report suggested Epic is pivoting to an AI first development model for an upcoming Star Wars and Marvel-themed shooter, and Tim Sweeney said developers are being moved to retool for maximum AI acceleration.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Epic's leadership frames AI as a company-wide transformation, relevant to game development cost structures and Unreal adopters.
insights.quote: We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration

insights.claim: Sweeney says the aim is not to do the same with fewer people but to enable everyone to build more and better, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Epic is signaling AI tooling will come to the Unreal ecosystem, a potential product catalyst.
insights.quote: The aim isn’t to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff
